record.title: STMicroelectronics LSM6DSV16X - 6-axis IMU with on-chip sensor fusion (SFLP), LGA-14L
record.origin_why: Every figure in electrical.chip.json was read off ST's own datasheet DS13510 Rev 4 (May 2023), fetched 2026-09-02 from st.com itself (not a mirror) and hashed in PROVENANCE.json as datasheet.pdf; lifecycle was read off ST's product page the same day. No standard defines the part; nobody here has measured one. The folder carries NO geometry yet (cad/part.py is the triad skeleton) - a package body would be a derived asset with its own provenance line, as ce-parts/LSM6DSOX did.
record.lifecycle_why: st.com product page https://www.st.com/en/mems-and-sensors/lsm6dsv16x.html fetched 2026-09-02 (HTTP 200, 286536 bytes; not kept - a live page): status badge reads 'Active' with tooltip 'Product is in volume production.' A reading dated 2026-09-02, not a promise.
record.why: THE CHIP IS SOURCED; THE PART THE ROBOT CARRIES IS NOT. The Microduck has this chip on Pollen's imu_to_dxl v2 board, and that board's schematic, MCU, strapping and firmware are unpublished - so how the chip is wired, clocked and read (SA0, I2C/SPI, ODR, SFLP ODR, the FIFO word format robotd decodes as fp16) is CANNOT DETERMINE from the datasheet, which is exactly what electrical.chip.json says in nine recorded unknowns. cad/interfaces.json is empty (no geometry modelled yet), so bin/triad check has nothing to measure there either.
